chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jazzaki who said:
I asked Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'Should I pay the tenth of my wealth to the children of my daughter?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem.'

key_terms.عُشْرَ: Tenth (a specific tax or tithe, distinct from Zakat in some contexts but often used similarly for wealth)

ai.seo_question: Can I give my Ushr (tenth tax) to my daughter's children?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the permissibility of giving Ushr (the tenth portion of wealth) to one's daughter's children is confirmed, highlighting the Shia juristic view that maternal lineage does not disqualify descendants from receiving Zakat or Ushr. This ruling underscores the principle of 'tadkhil al-qarabah' (including relatives) and distinguishes Ushr recipients from the specific exclusions found in the Quranic verse 9:60, thereby facilitating wealth circulation within the extended family structure.
